question: Why do the action-based means become countless in practice?
premises: The action-based means contain many subsidiary methods.
These methods are divided according to inner and outer objects.
Their divisions and subdivisions multiply into great variety.
inference: Therefore the action-based means become countless in their internal forms.
uncertainties: avāntarāt is read as referring to internal or subsidiary differentiation.
plain_english: Within the means based on action, the methods are divided by inner and outer objects. Because of their many divisions and subdivisions, they become countless.
